prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your neighborhood, budget, system size, timeline and whether you want a high-efficiency install, heat-pump, duct work changes, etc. I can, however, help you pick a great contractor and find top local options if you share your ZIP code. Before that, here’s a quick plan and a few contractor names to consider.

If you want me to pull specific local companies and recent reviews, tell me your ZIP code. Otherwise use the guidance below.

How to choose the best HVAC company for an AC replacement
- Get at least 3 written bids (so you can compare scope and price).  
- Require a proper load calculation (Manual J) — not just “nameplate tonnage.”  
- Verify license, insurance and permits (ask for license number and proof of liability/workers’ comp).  
- Prefer NATE‑certified technicians and factory training for the brand they’re installing.  
- Ask about warranties (manufacturer + labor) and whether they’ll register the manufacturer warranty.  
- Confirm they’ll match indoor coil/air handler to the condensing unit, and check ductwork if needed.  
- Ask for SEER rating and estimated seasonal energy cost.  
- Get details on refrigerant type (R‑410A vs alternatives), disposal of old unit, timeline, and cleanup.  
- Check reviews and references (Google/Yelp/Angi/BBB) and look for recent complaints/resolutions.  
- Beware of very low bids, high-pressure sales, or contractors who won’t provide a written scope.

Typical questions to ask a contractor
- Do you perform a Manual J and provide the report?  
- Who will be doing the work (employees or subs)? Are they NATE‑certified?  
- What brand/models do you recommend and why? Estimated SEER and warranty?  
- What’s included (thermostat, disconnect, pad, permits, labor, start-up)?  
- Do you offer financing/maintenance plans?

Reputable companies to consider (have Atlanta presence or franchise locations)
- Coolray Heating & Air Conditioning (regional, large presence around Atlanta)  
- One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning / Benjamin Franklin (franchise with local Atlanta service)  
- ARS / Rescue Rooter (national chain with HVAC services locally)  
- Aire Serv (franchise network; local offices in many Atlanta suburbs)

(These are examples of well-established companies with local branches; check the specific Atlanta branch’s reviews and credentials.)

Ballpark cost and timeline
- Typical full central AC replacement for a single‑family Atlanta home: roughly $3,000–$8,000+ depending on system size and efficiency; specialized installs or ductwork can raise cost.  
- Most installs take 1–3 days; complicated jobs longer.

Red flags
- No written estimate or vague scope.  
- Contractor asks for full payment up front in cash.  
- Push to buy an oversized unit or refuses to perform a Manual J.  
- No proof of insurance or local license.

If you want, tell me:
- ZIP code or neighborhood, home square footage, how old your current system is, and any budget/efficiency goals — and I’ll find 3–5 well‑rated local contractors and help you compare their quotes.
